name: Fruit Fly (Cucurbit Fruit Fly)
description: A major pest of cucurbit crops (watermelon, cucumber) whose larvae feed inside fruits. The female punctures fruit to lay eggs, causing rot, fruit drop, and total loss of affected fruits. It is a significant constraint to cucurbit production in West Africa.
symptoms: Small puncture marks on fruit surface (egg-laying sites)
Soft, sunken, discolored areas around punctures
Fruit rot starting from oviposition sites
treatments: Use protein bait sprays (mixing insecticide with protein attractant) spot-applied on crops
Set up pheromone traps or methyl eugenol traps for male annihilation
Remove and destroy infested fruits — bury deep (>50cm)
Apply neem-based repellents during fruit development
Bag fruits with paper bags or netting to prevent egg laying
prevention: Practice field sanitation — remove all fallen and infested fruits
Use male annihilation technique with lure traps
Release sterile fruit flies in large-scale programs if available
Intercrop cucurbits with repellent plants (mint, basil)
Practice crop rotation with non-cucurbit crops
references: NAERLS Watermelon and Cucumber Pest Management
